```{r, include = FALSE}
# the full examples run when the package is built; CRAN checks skip them for time
has <- function(p) requireNamespace(p, quietly = TRUE)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = identical(Sys.getenv("NOT_CRAN"), "true") && has("posterior") && has("bayesplot") && has("loo") && has("rstantools"),
                      collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4)
```

```{r setup}
library(bayescompR)
# chains run in parallel on this many cores; on your own machine use
# options(mc.cores = parallel::detectCores())
options(mc.cores = 2)
```

A `bayescomp_fit` works with the packages built around rstan and CmdStanR:
posterior for draws and summaries, bayesplot for plots, loo for model
comparison and rstantools for the generics of model packages. Packages
that write Stan programs (brms, rstanarm, multinma) can hand them to
bayescompR, which then fits them without a C++ toolchain.

## A model to work with

```{r}
code <- "
data {
  int<lower=0> N;
  vector[N] x;
  array[N] int<lower=0> y;
}
parameters {
  real alpha;
  real beta;
}
model {
  alpha ~ normal(0, 2);
  beta ~ normal(0, 1);
  y ~ poisson_log(alpha + beta * x);
}
"
set.seed(10)
N <- 60
x <- rnorm(N)
y <- rpois(N, exp(0.5 + 0.4 * x))
y[N] <- 25 # one outlier
model <- bayescomp_model(code, data = list(N = N, x = x, y = y))
fit <- bayescomp_sample(model, chains = 4, iter_warmup = 500, iter_sampling = 500,
                        seed = 1, refresh = 0)
```

## posterior

`posterior::as_draws()` and its `_array`, `_df` and `_matrix` variants
return the post warmup draws; `bayescomp_as_draws()` does the same.
Everything in posterior then applies.

```{r}
d <- posterior::as_draws_df(fit)
posterior::summarise_draws(d, "mean", "sd", ~quantile(.x, c(0.05, 0.95)), "rhat", "ess_bulk")
posterior::summarise_draws(posterior::as_draws_df(fit, "beta"), posterior::default_convergence_measures())
```

## bayesplot

`bayesplot::nuts_params()` returns the sampler diagnostics in the long
format the NUTS plots expect, and `bayesplot::log_posterior()` the `lp__`
draws.

```{r}
a <- posterior::as_draws_array(fit)
bayesplot::mcmc_trace(a, pars = c("alpha", "beta"))
bayesplot::mcmc_scatter(a, pars = c("alpha", "beta"), np = bayesplot::nuts_params(fit))
bayesplot::mcmc_nuts_energy(bayesplot::nuts_params(fit))
```

## Posterior predictive checks without generated quantities

`bayescomp_posterior_predict()` draws replicated data from every sampling
statement on data in the model block, using the matching `_rng`
function, and `bayescomp_log_lik()` returns the pointwise log likelihood.
A generated quantities block is not needed for either, and
`rstantools::posterior_predict()` and `rstantools::log_lik()` fall back
to them when the fit has no `y_rep` or `log_lik` variable.

Each sampling statement or `target +=` of a density on data in the model
block contributes one column per element of its left side; a
multivariate statement contributes one column for the whole statement.
Truncated statements are not supported, and posterior predictive draws are
`NA` for a density without an `_rng` function.

```{r}
ll <- bayescomp_log_lik(fit)
dim(ll)   # draws by observations
yrep <- bayescomp_posterior_predict(fit, seed = 2)
dim(yrep)
bayesplot::ppc_dens_overlay(y, yrep[1:50, ])
bayesplot::ppc_stat(y, yrep, stat = "max")
```

## loo

`loo::loo()` uses the generated quantity `log_lik` when the program has
one, and otherwise the pointwise terms of the model block, with relative
efficiencies computed from the chains.

```{r}
lo <- loo::loo(fit)
lo
```

The outlier has a large Pareto k, so its PSIS estimate is unreliable.
`bayescomp_reloo()` refits the model without each such observation and
replaces its estimate with the exact leave one out predictive density.
It needs a function that returns the data with observation `i` removed.
The held out density is evaluated with the full data model at the draws of
the refit, so the parameters must not depend on the number of
observations:

```{r}
drop_obs <- function(i) list(N = N - 1L, x = x[-i], y = y[-i])
lo_exact <- bayescomp_reloo(fit, drop_obs, lo, k_threshold = 0.7, refresh = 0)
lo_exact$refits
lo_exact
```

Models are compared with `loo::loo_compare()` as usual:

```{r}
code_nb <- sub("real beta;", "real beta;\n  real<lower=0> phi;", code, fixed = TRUE)
code_nb <- sub("y ~ poisson_log(alpha + beta * x);",
               "phi ~ exponential(1);\n  y ~ neg_binomial_2_log(alpha + beta * x, phi);", code_nb, fixed = TRUE)
fit_nb <- bayescomp_sample(bayescomp_model(code_nb, data = list(N = N, x = x, y = y)),
                           chains = 4, iter_warmup = 500, iter_sampling = 500, seed = 1, refresh = 0)
loo::loo_compare(list(poisson = lo_exact, negbin = loo::loo(fit_nb)))
```

## brms

brms writes a Stan program and its data with `make_stancode()` and
`make_standata()`. Both go straight into `bayescomp_model()`:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
library(brms)
f <- bf(count ~ zAge + zBase * Trt + (1 | patient))
scode <- make_stancode(f, data = epilepsy, family = poisson())
sdata <- make_standata(f, data = epilepsy, family = poisson())
m <- bayescomp_model(scode, data = unclass(sdata))
fit_brms <- bayescomp_sample(m, chains = 4, seed = 1)
summary(fit_brms, c("b_Intercept", "b", "sd_1"))
```

The loops brms writes for linear predictors (`mu[n] += r_1_1[J_1[n]] *
Z_1_1[n]`) are vectorized by the compiler, so these models run 10 to 30
times faster than the loops would. The draws use brms's internal
parameter names; `brms` itself is not needed to fit or summarize them.

## rstanarm and multinma

rstanarm and multinma ship compiled models and pass their Stan program
and data to `rstan::sampling()`. A small function, run in your own
session, captures both instead of sampling:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
capture_stan <- function(expr) {
  # the tracer runs at the start of rstan's sampling method, where 'object'
  # is the compiled model and 'data' the data list, and stops it there
  options(captured_stan = NULL)
  trace(rstan::sampling, signature = "stanmodel", where = asNamespace("rstan"), print = FALSE,
        tracer = quote({
          options(captured_stan = list(code = object@model_code, data = data))
          stop("captured")
        }))
  on.exit(untrace(rstan::sampling, signature = "stanmodel", where = asNamespace("rstan")))
  try(expr, silent = TRUE)
  getOption("captured_stan")
}

library(multinma)
net <- set_agd_arm(smoking, study = studyn, trt = trtc, r = r, n = n, trt_ref = "No intervention")
s <- capture_stan(nma(net, trt_effects = "random", prior_intercept = normal(scale = 100),
                      prior_trt = normal(scale = 100), prior_het = normal(scale = 5)))
m <- bayescomp_model(s$code, data = s$data)
fit_nma <- bayescomp_sample(m, chains = 4, seed = 1)
```

rstanarm's Gaussian models call `CODOLS()`, a function rstanarm
implements in C++. Supply it in R with the `functions` argument:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
library(rstanarm)
s <- capture_stan(stan_glm(mpg ~ wt + hp, data = mtcars))
codols <- function(X, y) qr.coef(qr(X), y)
m <- bayescomp_model(s$code, data = s$data, functions = list(CODOLS = codols))
```

## rstantools

`rstantools::log_lik()` and `rstantools::posterior_predict()` return
draws by observations matrices with the chains stacked, the format model
packages use:

```{r}
dim(rstantools::log_lik(fit))
dim(rstantools::posterior_predict(fit))
```

Package authors who build on bayescompR rather than rstan can call
`bayescomp_model()` on a program stored in `inst/stan` at run time; no
compilation step is needed when the package is installed.
